question: What is the distribution of within-cycle world-edge observation counts, and why does it concentrate at 1-4 rather than at the floor?
definition: A world edge's engine count in one processed reset group is the number of ordered source-then-target tag pairs within the engine's three-event lookback, restricted to edges in the world's training-edge set. The counts reset at the group boundary, but the event history does not: a current group can pair with the last two events of the previous group. The strict count uses only events in the same group. A withheld block-end event can make a group longer than the nominal eight events.

method.cells: the five zero-S_ever persistence-off cells and all seven non-zero off cells
method.cycles: processed reset groups from the committed world; 120 nominal cycles
method.window_definition: current event plus the two preceding events
method.count_unit: one ordered source-target tag pair in the lookback; not a distinct-edge count
method.primary_count: engine count with persistent event history and counts reset per group
method.secondary_count: strict count using only events in the same reset group
method.positive_control: eight events alternating the same two tags; the repeated-pair control must produce a count above 4

findings: The five zero cells have no reset group longer than 8 events; across 600 groups their engine counts are 1-4 and never 5.
Count 1 is the count in 0.8599 of zero-cell edge-cycle rows; count 2 in 0.1303, count 3 in 0.0095, count 4 in 0.0003.

Every count is an in-window source-target event pair: lag 0 supplies 0.0000 of zero-cell observations, lag 1 supplies 0.8587 and lag 2 supplies 0.1413. Cross-group lookback supplies 0.1527 of them but never lifts a zero group above 4.

Groups of at most 8 events have a maximum of 4 in both roles, even with cross-group lookback; the controls' 5-6 counts occur only in the 149 groups longer than 8, created when a withheld block-end event suppresses the reset.

Count 1 is the common case because each event contributes only two tags and most source-target pairs are seen once inside the three-event lookback; higher counts require the same two tags to recur in nearby events.

not_evidence: A descriptive distribution on six committed seeds, one world family and one persistence-off replay. It does not test a floor, change a floor, run a cell or claim that the 1-4 concentration is a general property of the engine. The split between short and merged groups is a record-arithmetic distinction, not a treatment, and the cross-group lookback is part of the committed replay rather than an added mechanism.
